chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Rifa'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman whose husband dies while he is absent, when should she observe her waiting period? He said: 'The day the news reaches her.' And he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One of you women used to remain for a year when her husband died and he was absent, then she would cast her desires behind her back.'
ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period begin for a widow if her husband dies while he is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that the waiting period (iddah) for a widow whose husband dies while absent begins upon the actual receipt of news, rather than a fixed duration from the date of death. It references a prophetic precedent where women observed a full year of mourning in such cases, highlighting the transition from extended customary mourning to the standardized four months and ten days prescribed in Islamic law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Rafa’at who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the one widowed from her husband and he is absent, when should she observe her waiting period from?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The day it (news) reaches her’. And he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘One of you women used to remain waiting for a year when her husband died and he was absent, then she would throw her desires behind her back’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Nasr from Rifa‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman whose husband dies and he is absent and about when she must begin counting her waiting period. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is from the day the news reaches her. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said to women, “One of you would wait for one year, when her husband died and he was absent, hold back her carnal desires and throw it behind her.’””
